scores.notes: The priest removes feathers from the bird over the heap of ashes beside the horned bronze altar in the tabernacle courtyard, matching Leviticus 1:16 without gore or extra faults.
Moses gestures from a rocky rise as the Israelites pack their camp beneath cloud-ringed Mount Horeb to begin their journey, with clean anatomy and no depiction-rule issues.
A bright beam of light from the sky shines around Saul on the road near walled Damascus while he shields his eyes and his companions recoil, accurately matching Acts 9:3.

A disembodied dark leather shoe sticks out on the grass beneath the empty left side of the tea table behind Alice's legs with no figure or leg attached to it. Otherwise the tea-party characters and setting match the passage.

Unreadable pseudo-script writing squiggles are clearly visible on the folded paper slip Holmes holds in the center and on a sheet protruding from the stack at bottom-right of the desk. The scene itself faithfully captures Lestrade leaning over to point at the other side of the bill while Watson watches.
Jesus stands in the fishing boat with right arm raised to rebuke the storm and waves while the frightened disciples watch, cleanly depicting Mark 4:39 with coherent anatomy and composition.

In the center background, the two hoisting ropes from the scaffolding pass contradictorily through a stone held overhead by one worker on their way to a second stone held by another worker, with a third loose rope end terminating straight up in mid-air. The foreground masonry work on Jerusalem's wall otherwise fits Nehemiah 3:9.

Young David crouches by the brook with his staff, sling, and stone-filled pouch selecting a smooth stone as armored Goliath and his shield-bearer advance across the stream, accurately matching 1 Samuel 17:40.

Ezekiel raises his hand to prophesy over the desert valley scattered with dry bones, with no figure drawn for God. Unpainted white paper appears along the left edge beneath the hillside and at the bottom-right corner, which is accepted by this item.
A massive cloud rests directly over the tabernacle in the center while the Israelites remain encamped in tents with their families and flocks around it, faithfully illustrating Numbers 9:22.

Holmes stands before the Baker Street window holding the sparkling blue carbuncle up to the light while Watson watches from an armchair, cleanly matching the scene with sound anatomy and no screen-adaptation likeness.
The Levite stands solemnly inside his stone house holding a knife beside his fully shrouded concubine, faithfully depicting Judges 19:29 while avoiding any gore.

The March Hare's left coat sleeve stretches behind the Dormouse's head while a separate tan furry hand emerges impossibly from his waistcoat right below the Dormouse's left-side ear. In addition, small unreadable dark glyph-like marks appear on the white paper card tucked into the Hatter's hatband.

Holmes studies Irene Adler's portrait through a magnifying glass in Baker Street while Watson observes from the fireside armchair, fitting the opening reflection cleanly with no lettering or anatomical defects.

On the right, the crowned King and the Knave are drawn as flat oblong playing cards with stick limbs instead of people in court-card dress, breaking the depiction rule, and ordinary metal wire croquet hoops and wooden mallets appear alongside the doubled-up card arches. Playing-card suit pips and small corner pips are visible on the cards, and a small white unpainted corner appears at bottom-right (accepted).

A seated, hooded human-shaped figure draped in white robes is depicted on the central fiery throne for God, violating neverDrawn and the depiction rule against giving God the Father a body or robe. A prominent kneeling narrator figure holding a staff is also added in the center foreground though not called for in Revelation 4:6.
Holmes pulls Watson into the Baker Street room while shutting the door as the stout, fiery-red-haired Mr. Wilson half rises from his armchair, matching the text cleanly with natural hands and poses.
Outside the temple gate, Peter grasps the lame beggar by the right hand to raise him up while John and temple-goers watch, accurately matching Acts 3:7 with clean anatomy.

A unified fresco-style lineage scene connects Abraham by his tent, crowned King David with his harp beneath a grapevine, and the infant Jesus with Mary and Joseph, clearly illustrating Matthew 1:1 without text or halo inscriptions.

Hatherley points excitedly toward the burning whitewashed house while holding his neatly bandaged left hand as Holmes, Watson, fire-engines, and a crowd look on, faithfully depicting the scene. Slight unpainted white paper shows at the top-left corner and margin, which is accepted.

Elderly Obed sits on a stone bench while Jesse stands beside him with his hand on young shepherd David's shoulder outside a Bethlehem house, cleanly depicting the three generations named in Ruth 4:22.
Jesus stands on the shore beside a glowing charcoal fire laid with fish and bread as Peter steps ashore and the other disciples haul in their net from the boat, accurately depicting John 21:9.
Disciples frantically wake Jesus on the cushion in the stern of the storm-tossed boat while others bail water and cling to the rigging, directly matching Mark 4:38 with solid anatomy.

A disembodied pink three-toed paw sticks straight up on the tablecloth beside the Dormouse's bread plate, and disproportionately huge grey furry legs and feet appear on the grass under the tiny Dormouse's armchair. Unpainted white paper edges at the right and bottom corners are accepted.

Besides the King of Hearts on the throne, two duplicate crowned, white-bearded Kings of Hearts in matching royal heart-patterned robes appear in the lower-left and lower-right foreground. A playing-card corner index 'K' and heart pips appear on the enthroned King's card tabard, along with faint unreadable marks on the Hatter's hat and White Rabbit's page.

Alice sits indignantly in a large armchair at one end of the tea table outside the house while the Hatter, sleeping Dormouse, and March Hare crowd the far end, matching the scene cleanly. Unpainted white paper margins along the bottom and right edges are accepted.

Unreadable pseudo-script lines of writing appear on the printed slip Watson holds up to the window light, on the stacked papers across the foreground desk, and on the sheets resting in Holmes's lap. Otherwise the Baker Street scene accurately depicts the passage.
King Darius presses his signet ring into clay over the stone slab covering the den while his lords wait with their own cylinder seals and guards stand behind, faithfully illustrating Daniel 6:17.
Ezekiel stands on a rocky ledge gesturing over a vast desert valley strewn with dry skulls and bones beneath dramatic lit clouds, matching Ezekiel 37:4 with no figure drawn for God.

The Caterpillar is given an overtly human face (with human eyes, nose, lips, and jowls) and uncalled-for human attire rather than an animal face, breaking the depiction rule for talking animals. In addition, a tiny doll-sized cottage sits in the foreground grass at bottom-right smaller than Alice despite her mushroom-sized scale.

Daniel watches from the right foreground as empty thrones surround a central throne of blazing flames and burning wheels before kneeling multitudes, honoring Daniel 7:9 without depicting a human figure for the Ancient of Days.

In the vaulted bank cellar stacked with crates, Holmes kneels with lantern and magnifying lens to inspect the flagstones while Watson looks on and Mr. Merryweather sits glumly on a crate. Slight unpainted white paper corners at top-left, bottom-left, and bottom-right are accepted.
The father embraces his ragged barefoot son while directing servants who bring forward the crimson robe, a ring on a cloth, and sandals, faithfully depicting Luke 15:22 with clean anatomy.

Alice's left bare forearm fuses directly into the King's left hand clutching her skirt, and in the right background a player uses a standard wooden croquet mallet, ball, and wire hoop instead of Wonderland croquet gear. Playing-card corner indices ('A', '10', inverted '6'/'g') and suit pips also appear on the King's tunic and background card soldiers.

Moses gestures from a rocky outcrop beneath cloud-ringed Mount Horeb as Israelite families travel onward with their livestock along the winding road, faithfully depicting Deuteronomy 1:7 with no figure drawn for God.
